_note: RC-1 (OPP-0003) placeholder answers for Flex Design, Engineering and Manufacturing Services (P-49 part B). ILLUSTRATIVE, not real Flex positions: no test result, capacity figure or certification here is verified.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: We would build and deliver a system-level simulation of the power chain covering dynamic response, source output impedance, module current sharing, distribution inductance and ripple, calibrated against our module and rack test results. We would also give the electrical design lead the models and measured data needed for the DC arc-flash and fault-current studies.
answers.conditions: Model parameters for the converters and distribution come from the power units and the Owner's design consultant.
answers.next_steps: Agree the simulation tool, model boundaries and data exchange with the power units during the dialogue.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: The same system-level simulation, covering dynamic response, source output impedance, distribution inductance and ripple, would be submitted for the Owner's acceptance well before delivery, together with the test data used to validate it.
answers.conditions: The Owner's review period is scheduled ahead of the technical decision point (DL-04).
answers.next_steps: Propose a submission date for the simulation in the project plan.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: We would run a witnessed factory test on the first unit of each type and factory acceptance tests on repeat units, including power up and down, monitoring, reset, console power cycling, failover, resilience and a 72-hour constant-load run, and then support site acceptance and commissioning. Step-load, pulse-profile, ride-through, protection and ground-fault tests would be done at rack and module level in the factory, with the block-scale and end-to-end tests from MV input to the GPU done on site.
answers.reason: Factory test bays cannot draw a full power block's load or hold the complete MV-to-GPU chain, so block-scale pulse profiles and end-to-end validation can only be shown at site acceptance.
answers.conditions: Benchmarks are run with the Cloud unit's software stack.
answers.next_steps: Agree with the Owner which TA-06 tests are factory and which are site tests in the acceptance test plan.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: We would receive, inspect and integrate the Owner-furnished equipment into our integration and test plan, with interface checks before installation so it fits the overall data center design.
answers.conditions: The Owner provides data sheets, interface drawings and delivery dates for its equipment.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: We would train the Owner's operators and maintainers on the test procedures, fault diagnosis and spare-part handling for the equipment we build and test, delivered before acceptance.
answers.next_steps: Agree the training plan and number of trainees in the dialogue.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: We note that the Owner publishes PUE per cooling technique and the energy price during the dialogue, and we would use these figures in our cost inputs to the total cost of ownership.

Illustrative placeholder response: We would support our scope for five years from acceptance, 24 by 7, with a four-hour response, concurrent maintenance and six hours for cabinet-level concurrent repairs, backed by on-site spares and our repair and failure analysis centre. For other repairs we propose restoring service within 2 hours rather than completing the repair.
answers.reason: A full board-level repair, including re-test, cannot be completed within 2 hours on site.
answers.workaround: Restore service within 2 hours by swapping field-replaceable units from on-site spares; the failed unit is repaired and re-tested at our repair centre and the spare restocked within an agreed turnaround.
answers.next_steps: Size the on-site spares holding with the Owner.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: Our integration and test lines can build the core components first and ship a test system with a minimal management stack soon after contract signing, followed by the phased deliveries.
answers.conditions: The test system configuration is agreed at contract signature.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: We would run the factory tests and support each acceptance step through to the 30-day availability test, with our deliverables timed against award and first delivery.

Illustrative placeholder response: We would agree the pre-delivery assembly, quality assurance and factory test plan at least 30 days before the factory test, covering burn-in, benchmarks and fault injection such as cable disconnects, subsystem power-downs and known bad parts.

Illustrative placeholder response: Our test engineers would support the 60-day acceptance period on site, including the functionality demonstration, the two cold boots, fault-injection resilience tests and the 30-day availability test.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: Our prices would be firm for every phase, all-inclusive, quoted in US dollars free of taxes, cover delivery, installation, commissioning and training, and be split into equipment, freight, installation, commissioning, spares and five years of maintenance, with any extension priced as an option. A capped adjustment on a short list of named components against published market indices is offered only as an alternative in the commercial exceptions schedule.
answers.next_steps: Price the component risk into the firm price and agree the alternative's component list with the bid manager.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: Our prices would be unconditional, with no 'to be discussed' items or references to a separate contract; the indexed price appears only as an alternative in the exceptions schedule.
Illustrative placeholder response: Our offer would stay valid for at least four months after the submission deadline.

Illustrative placeholder response: If awarded, we expect to provide the 10% performance guarantee at signature, a pre-financing guarantee of up to 30% if pre-financing is requested, and performance and payment bonds in a form the Owner approves.

Illustrative placeholder response: We accept liquidated damages for missed service levels, capped by the at-risk amounts described, and delay penalties that scale with the length of the delay and the seriousness of the breach, subject to an aggregate cap on liquidated damages and delay penalties together.
answers.reason: Liquidated damages and delay penalties have no overall limit as written, which leaves an open-ended risk on a phased multi-lot delivery.
answers.workaround: An aggregate cap on liquidated damages and delay penalties together, set as a percentage of each lot's price; the percentage is stated in the financial offer and listed in the commercial exceptions schedule (CT-08).

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: Our commercial exceptions are listed in the separate exceptions schedule and kept to a minimum: on liquidated damages, only the aggregate cap per lot asked for under CT-07; any indexed price is shown there only as an alternative to the firm price.

Illustrative placeholder response: Warranty on our scope would run within the five-year maintenance period, with component warranties inside it, and we accept responsibility for failures caused by disturbances foreseeable within the Section 9 interface limits.

Illustrative placeholder response: We provide a supply-chain security and risk plan for each component in our scope, with approved alternate sources, traceability and mitigation for sensitive parts. Instead of a guarantee for each original component over the system's whole lifetime, we commit to the availability period stated as the proposed change.
answers.reason: No supplier can guarantee every original component for an open-ended system lifetime: electronic parts follow their makers' life cycles.
answers.workaround: Spare parts or compatible form-fit-function replacements available for at least 10 years from acceptance, with at least 12 months' notice of end of life and a last-time-buy offer before any component is discontinued.
